question: I'm hunting compounders: 3-year revenue CAGR above 20%, EPS CAGR above 25% (so earnings growing faster than sales — margin leverage), ROE consistently over 20%, and net debt/EBITDA under 2x. Global, any sector.

_conventions._note: For the fields below, read the `definition` and/or `sign` before interpreting the value — a negative can MEAN something (an outflow, a benefit) and an ambiguous name needs its definition. Every other field is a plain magnitude.

eps_diluted.definition: PER SHARE, in the company's REPORTING currency (NOT USD-normalized like the _usd fields) — don't mix it with the USD amounts.

answer_to_user: Compounder screen, global, all sectors, all conditions intersected: 3-year revenue CAGR > 20% (compound_growth, N=3, thr 0.20), 3-year EPS CAGR > 25% (compound_growth, N=3, thr 0.25 — so EPS compounding faster than sales = margin/operating leverage), ROE sustained > 20% every year (sustained_above, N=3), AND net_debt/EBITDA < 2x (net debt, not gross). 60 matches. Top: NVIDIA, Eli Lilly, Arista, Amphenol, 6669.TW, Vertiv. The EPS-CAGR (25%) > revenue-CAGR (20%) thresholds encode the 'earnings growing faster than sales' quality insight; every metric carries per-row evidence and both CAGRs use the same 3-year window.
